newsitem.title: USA: Dow slips to narrow loss ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Dow slips to narrow loss ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: U.S. blue chips closed slightly lower on Monday after a session that saw investors adopt a cautious stance ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy committee meeting.
The Dow fell seven points to close unofficially at 6806. Broader indices were little changed, with the S&P 500 managing a fractional advance and the Nasdaq Composite edging lower.
"It's like hurry up and wait time," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital.
Very few economists believe the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee will vote to increase interest rates at its meeting, which starts Tuesday and concludes Wednesday.

But even so, analysts said, investors seemed content to wait for the outcome of the meeting. Several analysts noted stocks may well remain in a holding pattern until Friday, when the critical U.S. monthly employment and wage report is due.

"The fact is the economy is in very good shape and the major point is to what extent are labor costs accelerating," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "The wage portion of the employment report holds that secret."
Recent data confirmed the economy enjoyed robust growth in the fourth quarter of 1996. Just as important, however, have been indicators that showed no sign of runaway inflation.
Early Monday, the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) released its index of manufacturing activity.

The overall index fell to 52.0 in January from a revised 53.8 reading in December while its price component rose to 51.4 in January from 50.8 a month ago, neither of which suggested an inflation threat.
Bonds rose after the release of the NAPM report and then settled into a tight range, leaving interest rates slightly lower at the end of the day.

Financial stocks were able to muster some momentum from the bond market's gains. Citicorp rose two points to 118-3/8, Chase Manhattan Corp gained 1-1/4 to 93-3/4 and BankAmerica Corp rose 1-5/8 to 113-1/4.
Among individual issues, Kysor Industrial Corp shares jumped 5-5/8 to 42-5/8 after the company agreed to a buyout by Scotsman Industries Inc.
Scotsman, which agreed to pay $43 cash for each Kysor share, rose 2-1/8 to 26-1/8.
In a related deal, Kuhlman Corp agreed to buy the assets of Kysor's transportation products group for $86 million cash plus the assumption of certain liablities. Shares in Kuhlman rose 1/2 to 18-1/4.
Transocean Offshore Inc slid 5-1/2 to 60 after warning its fourth-quarter earnings per share would fall $0.15 to $0.20 short of analysts' estimates, which averaged about $0.55.
New York Bagel Enterprises Inc skidded 2-1/8 to 4-5/8 after the company said its fourth-quarter earnings would fall short of what analysts had expected.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 3.80 points to 1376.05.
The Standard & Poor's 500 index rose 0.57 to 786.73.
